summary.text: Kathy Jennings is Delaware's Democratic Attorney General, first elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022, and won re-election on November 3, 2026.
A former Delaware state prosecutor, she has said her priorities are public safety, consumer and corporate accountability, election protection and legal action against federal policies.

paragraphs.text: Jennings was born and raised in Wilmington and graduated from the University of Delaware and Villanova University Law School.

Jennings began her career as a prosecutor in the Delaware Department of Justice, one of two women prosecutors there at the time, and later served as State Prosecutor and Chief Deputy Attorney General.
In 2017 she was appointed Chief Administrative Officer of New Castle County.
Jennings was elected Attorney General in 2018, the first woman Democrat elected to the post according to her survey response, and took office on January 1, 2019.
Kathy Jennings won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election for attorney general with 63.6% of the vote to David Graham's 36.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
